fixes.explanation: Yes, Father. God says of Solomon, “…and I will be his Father.” David passes along the words just as he heard them. Put together, the verse reads, “…I have chosen him as My son, and I will be his Father.”

That's it, friend. David says it was in his heart to build a house as a resting place for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and as a footstool for our God. He wasn't just daydreaming with his feet up, either. He tells the crowd he'd already gotten ready to build it.

David never brings up a wall in this speech. He says it was in his heart to build a house as a resting place for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and a footstool for our God. The building he talks about is that house, friend.
Close, but David says the opposite. In verse 2 he says, “I had made preparations to build it…” so he'd already started getting ready. He wasn't just wishing, friend. He was already working on it.

Age never comes up in what God says. The reason David gives is that he is a man of war who has shed blood. God said, “You are not to build a house for My Name, because you are a man of war who has shed blood.” So the reason is about David's past as a man of war, not about how many years he has.

Benjamin is a real tribe of Israel, and Saul, the son of Kish, came from it (1 Samuel 9:1-2). But David says God chose Judah as leader. From the house of Judah, God chose his father's household, and from there, David himself.
Yes, son. God says of Solomon, “…for I have chosen him as My son…” That's not a small word to hear from God, friend. David is repeating it right there in front of the whole room.

You've got it, baker. David says to keep and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, “…so that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your descendants forever.” So the purpose he gives covers the land now and an inheritance for descendants later. He says it in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD.

True! David tells Solomon, “If you seek Him, He will be found by you…” He says it right after telling Solomon to know the God of his father and serve Him wholeheartedly. That's David's word to his son.

True! David tells Solomon, “Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you.” Notice that David says my God. He's handing his son the job of building the house, and he's telling him the LORD God is with him.

House is the word. David says the LORD will neither fail nor forsake Solomon “…before all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.” So the promise lasts all the way to the last bit of work. That's the stretch David names, friend.

Not a word about paychecks, friend. David says, “…every willing man of every skill will be at your disposal for the work.” Willing is the word that stands out. I'd take a crew that wants to be there over a crew watching the clock any day.
